notes: `packages` is both the watch list and the argument allowlist: /agent bump <pkg> only
accepts a name that appears here. That is what removes the shell-interpolation
surface — an argument that is not in this file never becomes a command.
`usage` is what lets the rules tier reach a verdict without a model. Without
imported_symbols the reachability question is unanswerable, and every affected
package lands in `uncertain` rather than in `act` or `watch`.
`pinned` should match the lockfile. If it does not, the version arithmetic is
answering a question about a version you are not running.
allowlist. They name the subset of `packages`, `watch.upstreams` and
`watch.feeds` that may be rendered onto the public surface (the Pages site).
The default for anything unlisted is NOT publishable, because publication is
irreversible: a repository that has been public cannot be made un-public, and
a name written to an append-only history can never be rewritten. Listing every
entry above is the demo's choice — it watches a handful of widely-used
packages and one public feed. An instance watching its own private packages
should list only what it is willing to publish, and an explicit empty list is a
valid deny-all rather than an error.
